v.why: A conv already on the direct 0->3 route makes an additional conv into node 2 more redundant.
Edge 0 conv feeding node 1 and then edge 2 already gives node 2 a conv-processed route, so edge 1 conv is substitutable.
Stacked convs along 0->1->2 compose a larger receptive field so the upstream conv gains value.
Without edge 1 the 0->1 branch is the only way to get a second route into node 2, so its conv carries more of the cell's capacity.
Without the direct 0->3 edge all signal must pass through node 1 or 2, so the edge 0 conv becomes more important.
A pooling edge 4 offers no learned features at the output, so the direct conv on edge 3 becomes the main feature extractor.
The identity shortcut on edge 3 supplies a clean signal and gradient flow, so a deeper conv on edge 5 adds less.
Two identity paths into the output are redundant and dilute the learned branches.
A 1x1 on edge 1 already provides channel mixing into node 2, so another 1x1 after node 2 is redundant.
Edges 4 and 5 both sum into the output node, so a conv on edge 5 already saturates output-side capacity.
